transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I took on this historical society fundraiser like I could handle the whole thing myself—started designing quilts, calling volunteers, making schedules, promising deadlines. I mean, I really couldn’t possibly get all of that done.
During this time when you were taking on all these projects, did you also notice your mood feeling unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable compared to your normal self?
At first I felt almost glowing, like every idea I had was wonderful. But if anybody questioned me, I got pretty snappish—like they were just standing in my way.

How long did this period of high energy and irritability last, and did it cause serious problems—like conflicts at work, financial trouble, or needing to be hospitalized—or was it more something others noticed but didn't disrupt your daily life much?
It went on for about five months, with me running full speed on that historical society project, before everything fell apart.
Before this five-month period, have you ever had an earlier episode of depression or a similar high-energy period at any point in your life?
I’m not really sure. Nothing like that stands out to me before this.
Have you ever gone through a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down, lost interest in things you normally enjoy, or had noticeably low energy?
Lately, yes. I used to really enjoy checking on my garden and working on my quilt entries, but now I look at the fabric or the seed catalogs and just... don’t feel much of anything.

During this recent low period, has it affected your ability to manage daily tasks—like getting out of bed, going to work, or caring for yourself—or have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or not wanting to be alive?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but... I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, and nobody had to deal with my mess anymore.

During this current low period, has it become difficult for you to manage everyday responsibilities—like getting out of bed, keeping up with basic hygiene, or going to work—because of how you're feeling?
Yes. My husband has had to take over the household routines. I stopped keeping my commitments with the historical society too—I just couldn’t face the people who were waiting on me.

During this depressive period, have you experienced any unusual perceptions—like hearing voices or seeing things others don't—or had any beliefs that others might consider strange or not based in reality?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I haven’t been hearing or seeing things, and I don’t think I have any unusual beliefs.
